If not, Delete can be driven by the GrafanaRuleIdentifier built in `getEditableIdentifier`, and Pause needs a prom-rule-based path.

Rule view link lost its `returnTo` parameter

The removed GrafanaRuleListItem built the link with `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo })`, where `returnTo` came from `createReturnTo()` (old GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx). The new component drops it. Users who open a rule from a filtered or searched list no longer return to that list state from the rule view; they land on the default list. Restore `const returnTo = createReturnTo();` and pass `{ returnTo }` again.

Comment's reason for the More button doesn't match the menu

The test says the More button stays "for other actions like viewing", but the menu has no View item. It stays because Copy link is always shown. The test also never checks that Delete/Pause are hidden or that Silence opens a drawer, so it would not catch either regression above.

applyTemplateVariables now runs 2–3 times on the same query, and it is not idempotent

`runSplitQuery` now calls `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, scopedVars, request.filters)` (line 299). `runSplitGroupedQueries` then sends these already-interpolated targets to `datasource.runQuery` (querySplitting.ts:180), which calls `super.query`. `DataSourceWithBackend.query` calls `applyTemplateVariables` again on every target, with the same `request.filters` (packages/grafana-runtime/src/utils/DataSourceWithBackend.ts:185). On the shard path it happens three times: `runShardSplitQuery` applies it (shardQuerySplitting.ts:52), passes the result to `runSplitQuery` (shardQuerySplitting.ts:163), which applies it again, and then the backend wrapper applies it a third time.

`applyTemplateVariables` is not safe to repeat (datasource.ts:1127-1130). It runs `templateSrv.replace` and then appends the ad-hoc filters, so each later pass:
- re-runs `templateSrv.replace` over text that was already substituted. That text includes ad-hoc filter values, which the first pass appends after replacing. If a variable value or ad-hoc value contains `$name` and a variable called `name` exists, it gets replaced. The query changes and nothing tells the user.
- appends the ad-hoc filters again. For stream-selector matchers `addFilterToStreamSelector` removes duplicates (modifyQuery.ts:494). For queries with a parser, `addFilterAsLabelFilter` (modifyQuery.ts:511-541) does not, so `{a="b"} | json` with ad-hoc `x=y` reaches Loki as `... | x=`y` | x=`y`` (three copies on the shard path). That is the query the Query Inspector shows.

Before this PR, the non-shard split path applied it once, in `super.query`. The shard path applied `interpolateVariablesInQueries` without ad-hoc filters, then the backend wrapper applied it once.

Fix: interpolate exactly once. One way is to interpolate only in `runShardSplitQuery`/`runSplitQuery` for the values the splitting logic reads (expr for `querySupportsSplitting`/`isLogsQuery`, step for `calculateStep`), and keep sending the raw targets to `runQuery`. Another is to stop the backend wrapper from re-applying for these sub-requests. Either way, `runSplitQuery` should not interpolate again when `runShardSplitQuery` calls it. The tests do not catch this because they mock `runQuery`. The assertion `toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5)` in shardQuerySplitting.test.ts:112 encodes the 1 + 4 repeated calls instead of the intended single interpolation.

Device limit is bypassed on the second request: the local cache is written before the store rejects the device

`tagDeviceUI` calls `a.localCache.SetDefault(key, ...)` (line 87) before `CreateOrUpdateDevice` (line 93). When the store returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, the cache entry stays. On the device's next request within 29 minutes, `tagDeviceUI` finds the key at line 83 and returns nil, so `TagDevice` returns nil and `Anonymous.Authenticate` (client.go:44-58) hands back an anonymous identity. So a device over the limit gets turned away once, and then has access for the cache TTL. That repeats every 29 minutes, and the device is never written to the DB, so it is never counted either. Fix: set the cache only after `CreateOrUpdateDevice` succeeds, or delete the key when it fails. Also add a service-level test that calls TagDevice twice past the limit; the new test in database_test.go only exercises the store.

Signature change breaks the wire graph that still provides ProvideAnonDBStore

`ProvideAnonDBStore` now takes `(db.DB, int64)`, but `pkg/server/wire.go:374-375` still lists `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore` and binds `anonstore.AnonStore` to it. Wire has no `int64` provider. Also, `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` no longer consumes `AnonStore` (impl.go:37,43), so the provider is unused. Either problem makes wire generation fail, and `wire_gen.go` is not checked in. Remove those two lines from wire.go (or provide the limit some other way), or the server will not build.

Count-then-insert is not atomic, so concurrent new devices can exceed the limit

`CountDevices` and the INSERT run in separate sessions with no lock. With N instances or concurrent requests, several new devices can all see `count < deviceLimit` and all be inserted. If the limit is meant to be strict (for example for licensing), do the count and insert in one transaction, or accept and document that it can overshoot a little.

Device tagging is now synchronous on the auth path even when no limit is configured

Before, `TagDevice` ran in a detached goroutine with its own 2-minute timeout. Now every anonymous request with a cache miss blocks authentication on DB writes. With a limit set, that is a COUNT plus an INSERT/UPDATE, even with the default `device_limit = 0`. When the limit is 0, the synchronous call only matters for its error, which is just logged (line 49). Consider keeping the asynchronous path when `cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit == 0` and blocking only when a limit is enforced.

What does a user over the limit see?

`ErrDeviceLimitReached` is a plain `fmt.Errorf` error. authnimpl/service.go:207-221 joins it into `authErr` and returns it unchanged. It is not an `errutil` error like `errCantAuthenticateReq` (service.go:46), so which HTTP status and message the middleware gives a blocked user is unclear to me. Is the intent a 401 that sends them to login, or an explicit "device limit reached" message? Declaring it with `errutil.Unauthorized("anonymous.device-limit-reached")` would make the response deterministic.

Requests without X-Grafana-Device-Id skip the limit entirely

`TagDevice` returns nil when the device ID header is empty (lines 119-122), and also when the IP fails to parse (125-129). `Authenticate` then grants anonymous access. Any client that leaves out the header (curl, scripts, a modified frontend) is never counted and never blocked. If the limit is meant as an enforcement boundary rather than a soft cap for the UI, say so in the config docs, or treat a missing header as limited once the limit is reached.

Field initialised to `undefined` without a type annotation

`anonymousDeviceLimit = undefined;` makes TS infer the field type as `undefined` (under strict null checks), not `number | undefined` like the interface. Reading `config.anonymousDeviceLimit` typed through the class then gives `undefined`. Annotate it: `anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined = undefined;`. Note too that the backend always sends an int64 (0 when unset, frontend_settings.go:195), so the value is never actually `undefined`.

Fallback chain depends on per-site default_locale, but the translation cache is process-wide

`FallbackLocaleList#[]` now puts `SiteSetting.default_locale` in the fallback chain. That setting is different on each multisite database, and an admin can change it at runtime. The LRU cache in `lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:72` is keyed only on `key + config.locale + backend.object_id`, and it holds the result after fallback (`translate_no_cache(key).freeze`, line 75).

Example: on a process serving site A (default `de`) and site B (default `es`), a `fr` user on A triggers a missing `fr` key. The cache stores the German fallback. A `fr` user on B then gets that German string from the cache. The same thing happens on a single site after an admin changes `default_locale`: users keep getting the old site locale's strings until LRU eviction pushes them out. Nothing in the logs or the UI shows this.

Before this change, the only fallback was `:en`, which is the same for every site, so the cache key was enough. Fix: add the fallback chain (or `SiteSetting.default_locale`) to the cache key, e.g. `k = "#{key}#{config.locale}#{I18n.fallbacks[config.locale].join}#{config.backend.object_id}"`.

Fallback locales are only loaded in controller requests; jobs and emails silently miss fallbacks

The translate accelerator loads locales lazily. `I18n.translate` only loads `config.locale` (`lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:68`), and a locale that isn't loaded gives the Simple backend nothing to fall back to. The only caller of the new `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` is `ApplicationController#set_locale`.

Sidekiq jobs never run it. `Jobs::Base` sets `I18n.locale = SiteSetting.default_locale` (`app/jobs/base.rb:151`), and `PostAlerter` switches to `I18n.with_locale(user.effective_locale)` (`app/services/post_alerter.rb:138`). If a key is missing in the user's locale and the site locale or `:en` hasn't been loaded in that worker yet, the notification text comes out as "translation missing: …". The accelerator then caches that string under `key+locale`, so later lookups get it too, including web requests that did load the fallbacks.

The PR body says it adds server-side fallbacks, but they only work reliably inside controller actions. Fix: load the fallback chain where translation happens, e.g. in `I18n.translate` replace line 68 with `I18n.fallbacks[config.locale].each { |l| ensure_loaded!(l) }`. That would also make the explicit call in `set_locale` unnecessary.

TestLogger.FromContext drops every log written through it

`FromContext` returns `NewTestLogger()`, which is a new, unrelated instance. Code that now logs through `logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)` (for example `LoggerMiddleware.logRequest` at logger_middleware.go:58) will never bump `InfoLogs.Calls` on the `TestLogger` a test injected. A test written against this fake would see zero calls and either fail for the wrong reason or end up asserting nothing. Returning `f` would keep the recorded logs visible to the test. `New` (line 18) already has the same pattern, so this is a judgement call. Still, `FromContext` is now the main logging path for the middleware, so it matters more here.

LoggerMiddleware now silently depends on ContextualLoggerMiddleware running before it

`logRequest` no longer adds `pluginId`, `endpoint`, `uname`, `dsName` or `dsUID` itself. Those attributes only show up if `NewContextualLoggerMiddleware()` sits earlier in the chain, which it does today (pluginsintegration.go:160-161). If the middlewares are reordered, or `NewLoggerMiddleware` is used without the contextual one, the "Plugin Request Completed" egress log loses these fields with no error. The old InstrumentationMiddleware doc spelled out its ordering requirement, and this PR removed that comment (metrics_middleware.go:24-25). A short comment on `NewLoggerMiddleware`, or on the middleware list, would keep the dependency visible.

No tests for the new contextual logger middleware or the refactored logger middleware

`instrumentContext` moved here from metrics_middleware.go, and `LoggerMiddleware` now takes all its plugin/request attributes from the context. Neither change has a test. The clientmiddleware package has no `contextual_logger_middleware_test.go` or `logger_middleware_test.go`. One test that runs a request through ContextualLogger → Logger and checks that the emitted log contains `pluginId`, `endpoint`, `dsUID` and `uname` would cover the behaviour this PR claims to keep. Note that the `TestLogger` fake can't observe this today (see the fake.go finding).

Test function still named after the old middleware

The middleware was renamed to `MetricsMiddleware` and the test now calls `newMetricsMiddleware` (line 78), but the test function is still `TestInstrumentationMiddleware`. Renaming it to `TestMetricsMiddleware` would match the new name.

Migration crashes when embed_category is unset or doesn't match a category

`execute(...)[0]['id']` assumes the join returns a row. A site_settings row exists only when an admin has changed the setting from its default (`embed_category: ''`, removed from config/site_settings.yml). The join also needs the value to match a category name exactly. In every other case the result is empty, and `[0]` raises (PG::Result IndexError, or nil['id']). The `category_id == 0` fallback on line 14 never runs, so the migration aborts on most installs. The same pattern on line 15 also fails if `uncategorized_category_id` has no row. Check `cmd_tuples`/`ntuples` before indexing, as line 19 already does.

Migrated hosts keep their scheme/path, so existing embeds stop working

The old `allows_embeddable_host?` normalised each entry with `URI(h).host` (removed lines in app/models/site_setting.rb), so values like `http://eviltrout.com` or `https://example.com/1234` worked. The removed specs tested exactly those values. The migration inserts each raw line with SQL and skips the model's `before_validation` stripping (app/models/embeddable_host.rb:5-8). `record_for_host` then compares `lower(host)` with the bare `uri.host` (app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17), so these sites start getting 'invalid referer host' after upgrading and nothing tells them why. On GNU sed (Linux), `-i ''` treats `''` as the script and the real expression as a filename, so updating an existing `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` fails. `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is relative to the caller's CWD, not the script's location, so running it from the repo root writes to the repo's parent directory. Migration warning contradicts the SQL

The header says the column is added "without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty", but the statement adds `DEFAULT NOW()`. Drop the stale Prisma-generated warning. Note too that every existing row gets the migration time as `updatedAt`, so "Last updated" will show the deploy time for legacy cache entries until they are refreshed.

Working-hours check rejects a slot that falls outside any one of the day's ranges, not outside all of them

`workingHours.find(...)` returns true (meaning "unavailable") as soon as one entry covering `slotStartTime.day()` does not contain the slot. A user can have several entries on the same UTC day, and `getWorkingHours` (packages/lib/availability.ts:76-124) creates one entry per availability row. It also adds an overflow entry on the next or previous day when hours cross UTC midnight (availability.ts:103-121). Take an organizer in America/Los_Angeles working Mon–Fri 9–17. That gives `[1020–1439]` on Mon–Fri plus `[0–60]` on Tue–Sat. A Tuesday 18:00 UTC slot falls outside `[0–60]` and is rejected, and a Tuesday 00:30 UTC slot falls outside `[1020–1439]` and is rejected too. So every weekday slot for that host disappears, and no error explains why. A split day such as 9–12 plus 13–17 breaks the same way. This now runs for every fixed host (line 488) and every round-robin host (line 513), because both spread `workingHours` from `userAvailability`. Reject the slot only when no matching entry contains it, e.g. `workingHours.some(wh => wh.days.includes(day) && start >= wh.startTime && end <= wh.endTime)`, applied only when the user has an entry for that day.

A date with two or more override ranges blocks every slot on that date

`dateOverrides.find` returns true (unavailable) for any override on the slot's date whose range does not contain the slot. A user can set several time ranges for one override date, and `getUserAvailability` (packages/core/getUserAvailability.ts:215-224) creates one entry per range. With ranges 09–12 and 14–17, a 10:00 slot is "before" the 14–17 range (line 118), and a 15:00 slot is "after" the 09–12 range (line 123). So both are rejected and the host shows no availability that day. Collect the overrides for the slot's date first, then reject only if the slot fits inside none of them.

Working-hours `end` is computed from the slot start, so slots that run past the end of working hours pass

`end` is `slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()`, the same value as `start`. For hours ending at 17:00, a 60-minute slot at 16:30 passes `end > workingHour.endTime`. For round-robin hosts, `getSlots` builds slots from everyone's combined hours, so another host's later hours can produce that 16:30 slot, and it then gets assigned to this host. Use `slotEndTime` here.

Override bounds check accepts slots that only partly overlap the override

A slot is rejected only if it ends at or before the override start (lines 117-121), or starts strictly after the override end (line 123). So with an override of 09:00–12:00, a 60-minute slot at 08:30 or at 11:30 counts as available. A slot starting exactly at 12:00 also passes, because `isAfter` is strict. For round-robin hosts these slots can come from other hosts' availability (see `buildSlots` in packages/lib/slots.ts:85-100). The check should require `slotStartTime >= start && slotEndTime <= end`.

`===` between two Dayjs objects is always false, so the start == end check never runs

`dayjs(...).add(...) === dayjs(...).add(...)` compares two newly created object references, which are never identical. The branch is meant for an override with no available time (start equals end), and it can never be reached. In that case a slot starting exactly at the override instant passes both later checks: it does not end before the start, and it does not start after the end. Such a slot is then accepted through `dateOverrideExist`. Use `.isSame(...)` or compare `.valueOf()`.

Override date is matched on the UTC calendar date, not the organizer's date

Lines 107-110 shift the override start to real UTC and compare its `YYYY MM DD` with the slot's UTC date. For organizers far from UTC, the override's local day spans two UTC dates. Example: a Los Angeles override on the 13th, 09:00–17:00 PST, is 17:00 on the 13th to 01:00 on the 14th UTC. Then (a) the 12th's 16:00–17:00 PST working-hour slots (00:00–01:00 UTC on the 13th) match the override date and are rejected as "before the override". (b) The override's own slots after 16:00 PST fall on the 14th UTC, so the override is ignored for them and they go through the working-hours path. Also, `dayjs(date.start).format()` formats in the server's local timezone, while `slotStartTime` is UTC. Compare both dates in `organizerTimeZone`, e.g. `slotStartTime.tz(organizerTimeZone).format("YYYY-MM-DD")` against `dayjs.utc(date.start).format("YYYY-MM-DD")` (the stored wall-clock date).

Converted override minutes wrap at midnight, so overrides that cross the invitee's midnight are dropped or shown on the wrong day

`startTime`/`endTime` are taken as `hour()*60+minute()` after adding the offset, so they wrap modulo 24h. But `activeOverrides` (line 206-208) still picks the override for the invitee day equal to the organizer's date, without the offset. Example: organizer in UTC with an override of 17:00–23:00, invitee at +5:30. The result is start=1350 and end=270, which `buildSlots` skips as invalid (line 68). Every slot of that override is lost. Example two: an override of 20:00–23:00 becomes 01:30–04:30. It is shown at 01:30 on the organizer's date, a day before the real time. Both start and end need to be shifted as instants, and the override assigned to the invitee day the shifted times fall on.

New test does not exercise the new availability checks

The only added case uses an IST schedule (03:30–11:30 UTC, which doesn't cross UTC midnight), a single override range, and a single fixed host. That is why it misses the defects above. Consider adding cases for: an organizer whose hours cross UTC midnight (e.g. America/Los_Angeles 9–17), a day with two working-hour ranges, an override date with two ranges, and a round-robin event with a date override, which the PR title targets.

The second `OR` branch deletes every `WorkflowReminder` with `retryCount > 1`, whatever its `method`. Today only this SMS cron increments `retryCount`, so no EMAIL or WHATSAPP rows are affected yet. Nothing tests that a failed schedule increments `retryCount`, that a row is deleted once it passes the threshold, or that a lock or a successful schedule does not count as a failure. Given the two data-loss paths above, a handler test that mocks `twilio.scheduleSMS` would catch regressions.

Returned SQL fragments with a top-level OR are not parenthesized

The org and team auth builders return `(A) OR (B)` with no outer parentheses (lines 171-174, 204-207). `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` makes `teamId` optional for every scope. So `{ scope: "team", userId, orgId }` now compiles. The PR deletes the `Caching` describe block. But `getAuthorizationConditions` and `getFilterConditions` still cache results in `cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions` (insightsBooking.ts:83-95), and nothing tests that behaviour now. Only one raw-SQL query actually runs against the database (user scope)

The new `ANY(${array})` fragments for org and team scope (insightsBooking.ts:164, 168, 201) are only checked as Sql object shapes (lines 295-299, 332-343). They are never run against Postgres. The single query that runs, `getBaseConditions`, uses user scope, so it never exercises the `ANY` array binding or the OR/AND grouping. Add a `$queryRaw` assertion for team or org scope with bookings that should and should not match. That would confirm the raw-SQL rewrite returns the same rows as the old Prisma `where` objects.

Google refresh now saves the zod SafeParse wrapper as the credential key

`parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the result of `safeParse`, which is `{ success, data }`. The old code used `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)`, which returns just the data. Line 100 now writes `{ success: true, data: {...} }` into `credential.key`. Sync mode returns a fetch Response, which has no `.data`

When sharing is on, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the raw `fetch` Response (`_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-15`). `res?.data` is then undefined, so `token.access_token` at line 95 throws a TypeError. HubSpot sync mode stores a fetch Response as the credential

In sync mode `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a `fetch` Response, not the `HubspotToken` that `createToken` returns. `expiresIn` is undefined, so `expiryDate` becomes NaN. Line 198 then writes the Response object (which serializes to `{}`) as `credential.key`, and line 202 sets an undefined access token. Without an error the stored credential is wiped, and the catch only logs. The sync response needs `json()` plus a mapping to the HubSpot token shape.

Zoho Bigin sends the credential id as the user id

`refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` passes the credential's id where the helper expects `userId` (`refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3,11`). Salesforce refreshes on every instantiation, then ignores the new token

`getClient` runs from the constructor and now refreshes the token unconditionally each time a `SalesforceCalendarService` is created, with no expiry check. That adds a token request per booking operation and risks Salesforce rate limits. The fresh token is also never used: line 106 still passes the old `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` to `jsforce.Connection`. This path also skips `refreshOAuthTokens`, so credential sync is not honoured here. Line 86's `statusText !== "OK"` check fails on HTTP/2 responses, where `statusText` is empty; use `response.ok`.

Computed keys in `minimumTokenResponseSchema` don't express "any key"

`[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both evaluate to the literal key `"[object Object]"`, so the second entry overwrites the first. The resulting schema is `{ access_token: string, "[object Object]"?: unknown }`. `z.object` strips unknown keys, so in sync mode `expires_in`/`expiry_date` and every other field are dropped. Zoom and Office365 then store tokens with no expiry: office365's `isExpired(expires_in)` check at line 279 and zoom's expiry handling don't get the field they need, which causes repeated refreshes or a broken key. Use `z.object({ access_token: z.string() }).passthrough()` (or `.catchall(z.unknown())`).

Placeholder refresh_token can overwrite the real one

When the response has no `refresh_token`, the helper writes the literal string "refresh_token". Office365 spreads the parsed data over the stored credentials (office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:264), so the user's real refresh token is replaced with "refresh_token" in the DB. If sync is later turned off, refreshes fail. Consider leaving the field unset so callers keep the stored value.

Webhook secret check: plain `!==`, any HTTP method, unhandled throws

This endpoint can write OAuth credentials for any user, and it is guarded only by a `!==` string comparison, which is not constant-time. Consider `crypto.timingSafeEqual`. The handler also accepts any method rather than only POST. Malformed bodies (`parse` at line 31), a wrong encryption key (`symmetricDecrypt` at line 58) and non-JSON plaintext (`JSON.parse`) all throw and return a generic 500 instead of a 400.

One failed SendGrid cancel stops the whole cancel batch, and the earlier rows are never deleted

The `try` wraps the whole `for` loop. If `client.request` throws for any reminder, the loop stops and `Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)` (line 74) never runs. Late cancellations can still send the reminder because the cancel waits for the cron

Booking cancellation, request-reschedule, edited steps and removed event types no longer cancel the SendGrid batch. They only set `cancelled: true`, and the 15‑minute cron cancels reminders due within the next hour (scheduleEmailReminders.ts:44-51). If a booking is cancelled less than about 15 minutes before a scheduled reminder, the cron either runs too late or first hits the `deleteMany` for past reminders (scheduleEmailReminders.ts:34-41). The attendee then gets a reminder for a meeting that was cancelled. Before this change the cancel was sent to SendGrid immediately. Consider cancelling immediately when `scheduledDate` is within the cron interval plus SendGrid's cancel lead time, and deferring only reminders further out.

try/catch around fire-and-forget async calls catches nothing

`deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async and are called inside `forEach` without `await`. A rejection would never reach this `catch`, so `log.error` here can never run. Both functions already catch their own errors. Drop the try/catch, or collect the promises and `await Promise.allSettled(...)` so the cancels finish before the request returns.

Reminder DB updates are no longer awaited before the response

Before this change the reminder `deleteMany` calls were added to `prismaPromises` and awaited at line 497. Now `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` (which do the DB update or delete) are started but never awaited. If the serverless function is frozen after it responds, a reminder may never be marked `cancelled`, and its email is then sent. The same applies in bookings.tsx:488-494 and the workflows.tsx update paths. Consider collecting the returned promises and awaiting them with the other `prismaPromises`.

Team admin check uses `&&`, so only owners pass

`isTeamAdmin` already matches role ADMIN or OWNER (packages/lib/server/queries/teams/index.ts:270), and `isTeamOwner` matches only OWNER (:292). Joining them with `&&` means a team ADMIN who isn't the organizer or an attendee gets FORBIDDEN. Calling `isTeamAdmin` alone is enough. Hosts of collective bookings are also left out: `bookingsProcedure` allows them (util.ts:34-43), but this check doesn't.

Blacklist and duplicate checks are case-sensitive

`blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased (line 71), but `guest` is compared as typed. Entering `Foo@x.com` gets past a blacklisted `foo@x.com`. The check against existing attendees is also an exact `===` match (line 76), so `Bob@x.com` is added as a second row for attendee `bob@x.com`. Lowercase both sides of each comparison.

Server accepts unbounded, duplicate guest lists

Only the dialog checks that emails are unique (AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26-29). The API schema has no dedupe and no maximum length. A request with `[a@x.com, a@x.com]` creates two attendee rows through `createMany` (handler.ts:100-104), and each row gets an email. The handler also lets any attendee call it (handler.ts:52-54). So anyone who has booked can send any number of addresses and have cal.com email all of them. Dedupe the list, lowercase it, and set a `.max()` on the array.

Emails are sent for the raw `guests` list, not `uniqueGuests`

`sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` uses the unfiltered input. A guest who was already an attendee, and so was filtered out at line 76, is still in `newGuests`. In `sendAddGuestsEmails` (email-manager.ts:541-542) that attendee gets a full `AttendeeScheduledEmail`, a new-booking confirmation, instead of the add-guests notice. Pass `uniqueGuests` instead.

Calendar update runs with the caller's credentials, and a failure after the DB write is unrecoverable

`EventManager` is built from `ctx.user`'s credentials, the same way editLocation does it (editLocation.handler.ts:97-105). But editLocation only lets organizers and collective hosts in (util.ts:30-44). Here an attendee or a team admin can be the caller, and their credentials don't own the booking's calendar references. So the organizer's calendar event probably won't get the new attendees. Also, `updateCalendarAttendees` (line 165) isn't wrapped in try/catch and runs after the attendees are already written (lines 92-106). If it throws, the user sees an error and no emails go out. A retry then filters every guest out as a duplicate and returns `emails_must_be_unique_valid`. Use the organizer's credentials (`booking.user.credentials` is already included), and catch or log calendar failures the way editLocation does (lines 109-114).

Validation error never clears

`setIsInvalidEmail(true)` is only reset by the Cancel button (line 91). The error stays after the user fixes the emails. It also survives a successful submit (onSuccess, lines 36-41, doesn't reset it) and closing the dialog with Escape or the overlay (`onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}`, line 61). The next time the dialog opens, it shows "Emails must be unique and valid" before the user has typed anything. Reset the flag on success, on any close, and on a valid submit.

Error fallback can never be used

`message` is a template string, so it's never empty, and `message || t("unable_to_add_guests")` always uses `message`. When `err.data` is missing, the toast reads "undefined: …". Server messages that aren't translation keys come through raw.

New guests are stored with an empty name

Each guest is created with `name: ""`. The emails then go to `" <email>"` (attendee-add-guests-email.ts:19, and the same in the scheduled email), and greetings and attendee lists show a blank name. Falling back to the email's local part would read better.

A backup code plus any non-empty totpCode logs in without the password

The password is only checked when `!credentials.totpCode` (line 121). Before this PR, sending a `totpCode` skipped the password check, but the TOTP branch still had to accept that code. Now the backup-code branch (line 131) comes first and replaces TOTP verification completely. So a POST to the credentials callback with `{email, password: "", totpCode: "x", backupCode: "<valid code>"}` skips the password at line 121, takes the backup-code branch, passes, and returns the user. NextAuth passes every request field into `authorize`. The result is that someone with a user's email and one leaked backup code gets a full session, with no password and no authenticator. Fix: reject requests that carry both `totpCode` and `backupCode`, or always verify the password on the backup-code path (for example, check `if (user.password && (!credentials.totpCode || credentials.backupCode))`, or verify the password inside the backup-code branch).

Backup codes are case-sensitive while the UI suggests uppercase

Codes are generated as lowercase hex (`crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex")`, setup.ts:61). The login check only strips dashes before `indexOf` (here and in disable.ts:61). The input placeholder is `XXXXX-XXXXX` (BackupCode.tsx:21), so a user who writes or types a code in uppercase gets `incorrect-backup-code` for a valid code, which is the one moment they have no other way in. Normalise with `.toLowerCase()` (and trim) before comparing, in both places.

Two concurrent logins can both use the same backup code

Consuming a code is a read (line 73), then an in-memory null (line 148), then an unconditional `prisma.user.update` (line 149). Two simultaneous requests with the same code both find it before either write lands, so both succeed, and the code is not really single-use. Consider a conditional update (e.g. `updateMany` with `where: { id, backupCodes: user.backupCodes }`, failing when the count is 0) or a transaction.

Dismissing the dialog on the backup-codes step leaves the switch showing 2FA as off

2FA is now enabled on the server before the codes are shown, but `onEnable()` (which calls `utils.viewer.me.invalidate()`, two-factor-auth.tsx:65-68) only runs from the Close button (line 269). If the user closes with Escape or a click outside, only `onOpenChange` runs (two-factor-auth.tsx:64). That just toggles `enableModalOpen`: the settings switch keeps showing 2FA as disabled, and `step` stays `DisplayBackupCodes`, so reopening the modal shows the old codes again. Call `onEnable()` (or invalidate) as soon as enable succeeds, or handle dismissal on this step the same way as Close.

"Please generate them in your settings" points to a feature that does not exist

Backup codes are only created by `totp/setup` (setup.ts:61-68), which refuses users who already have 2FA enabled (setup.ts:42-44). Users who enabled 2FA before this PR have `backupCodes = null`, and settings has no way to generate codes for them, short of disabling and re-enabling 2FA. The message sends them looking for an option that is not there. Reword it (e.g. "disable and re-enable two-factor authentication to generate backup codes") or add a regenerate action.

The BackupCode component's function is named TwoFactor

It is the default export, so imports work, but React DevTools and stack traces will show `TwoFactor` for this component, which is confusing next to the real `TwoFactor`. Rename it to `BackupCode`.

Crash when booking a Google Meet event with no destination calendar

`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` gives `undefined` whenever the event has no destination calendar. `handleNewBooking.ts:1063-1067` now sets `destinationCalendar: null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has one. The next line reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` with no optional chaining. So when `evt.location === MeetLocationType`, this throws a TypeError and the booking fails, when it should fall back to Cal Video. The old code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`. Fix: use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

Video booking references no longer store their credentialId

The old code was `credentialId: isCalendarType ? evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId : result.credentialId`, so video references (for example a Zoom or Daily result from `createVideoEvent`) kept `result.credentialId`. The new code is `isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`, which drops the credentialId for every non-calendar reference. Later updates or deletes that find the video credential through `reference.credentialId` can no longer link the meeting to its credential. Fix: keep `result.credentialId` in both branches, since `createEvent` now fills it for calendars as well.

Fallback calendar lookup in updateEvent/deleteEvent can never match

This fallback only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, and it then searches for `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId`, i.e. a calendar whose externalId is null or undefined. In practice it always returns `undefined`. Before this change it fell back to the destination calendar's externalId. Now, for references saved without `externalCalendarId` (older bookings), `events.update` is called with `calendarId: undefined` (line 261), and `deleteEvent` (line 317) quietly switches to `primary`. An event stored on a non-primary calendar is then not updated, or not deleted (the 404 is resolved silently at line 335). Fix: fall back to the destination calendar that matches this service's credential, or to `event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId`.

Org slug condition is inverted

The old code was `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })`: the slug was set directly only when team billing is disabled, and with billing enabled it went into `metadata.requestedSlug` until payment. The rewrite `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` reverses this. With billing enabled, the org gets its slug immediately, before payment, and also carries `requestedSlug`. Self-hosted instances without billing create orgs with no slug at all. Fix: `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`. Line 153 is correct as it stands.

Team members' non-Google calendars are written to the host's calendar id

For collective events, `createAllCalendarEvents` (EventManager.ts:339-370) now calls `createEvent` once per destination, each time with that member's credential. Google looks up its calendar by `credentialId`, but Office365 (this line), Lark (larkcalendar CalendarService.ts:128) and CalDAV (packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:156) always take `destinationCalendar[0]`, the main host's calendar. A member's Office365 credential then posts to `/me/calendars/<host's id>/events`, which fails, and CalDAV filters to a URL the member doesn't have, so nothing is created. Either way the event never appears on the member's calendar, and nothing tells them. Fix: pass `credentialId` and match on it, as Google does. Alternatively, `createEvent` in CalendarManager could pass `externalId` through.

Collective members' calendars are dropped when the organizer has no destination calendar

When neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` is set, `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` (line 1067). In that case `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` does nothing, and the destination calendars of the other collective hosts are silently thrown away. Fix: initialise the array as `[]` (or build it as `[...main, ...teamDestinationCalendars]`). Keep in mind that `createAllCalendarEvents` treats a non-empty array differently from the no-destination fallback.

Recurring cancellation repeats all deletes once per calendar reference

This recurring branch now sits inside `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)`. For each reference it deletes every remaining occurrence with all of the organizer's calendar credentials, and it ignores which credential the reference belongs to. A booking with N calendar references therefore issues N copies of the same deletes, and other team members' recurring events are never deleted. Consider running this branch once, outside the loop, and deleting per reference credential.

Dynamic users no longer select `organization`, and error status codes changed

The rewritten `loadUsers` drops `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` from the dynamic-user query, but `IsFixedAwareUser` (line 355) still declares `organization: { slug: string }`, so code that reads `user.organization` on dynamic bookings now gets undefined. Separately, the plain `Error` thrown for an empty `dynamicUserList` (line 728) does not match the `HttpError`/Prisma checks, so it comes back as a 500 "Unable to load users" instead of an empty list leading to the existing not-found handling. Also, `eventType.users` (line 755) lost its `|| []` fallback. Please restore the `organization` select and return a 4xx for the bad-input case.

The import() calls run eagerly, so app modules are not loaded lazily

Each property is set to `import("./x")`, and that call runs as soon as the object literal is evaluated. Any module that imports `@calcom/app-store` (videoClient, getCalendar, handlePayment, deletePayment, handleCancelBooking, bookings router) therefore starts loading all 28 app packages right away, the same as the old static imports did. The only differences are that the modules land in separate chunks and every lookup now has to be awaited. If the aim of "Async import of the appStore packages" is to load only the app that is actually used, store thunks instead (`applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`) and have the call sites do `await appStore[key]?.()`. A side effect of the eager form: if one app module fails to load, its promise rejects with no handler attached until someone looks up that key, so Node can report it as an unhandled rejection at startup.

The try/catch around forEach(async …) no longer catches getCalendar errors

Before this change, `getCalendar` was synchronous. If it threw (for example, a CalendarService constructor failing on a bad credential key), the `try` at line 124 caught the error and logged it at line 137. Now the callback is `async` and `forEach` drops the promises it returns. A failure in `await getCalendar(...)` becomes an unhandled rejection that `logger.error` never sees, and the deletions are not awaited before the reschedule email goes out. The same pattern was added in `packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts:125` and `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx:553`; the last one has no try/catch at all. A rejection from `deleteEvent` escaped in the same way before this change, so the gap already existed. Collecting the promises and awaiting them would fix both: `await Promise.allSettled(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (ref) => …))`.

Lithuanian totpStep1 replaced with Italian text

The new value `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:` is Italian (it matches `messages_it.properties:138` almost word for word), not Lithuanian. Simplified Chinese file now has a Traditional Chinese totpStep1

Java MessageFormat syntax in an i18next bundle breaks interpolation

This bundle is read by i18next (`js/apps/admin-ui/src/i18n/i18n.ts:13-34`). It uses the default `{{x}}` interpolation, and the neighbouring keys follow that convention (`error-invalid-length='{{0}}' must have a length between {{1}} and {{2}}.` at line 2995). Changing `{{0}}` to `{0}` and adding `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}` means the admin console will show the literal placeholders and the raw choice pattern instead of the attribute name and limits. The same change was made in `js/apps/account-ui/maven-resources/theme/keycloak.v3/account/messages/messages_en.properties:188`, which is loaded by i18next with default interpolation (`js/apps/account-ui/src/i18n.ts:25-43`). I found no step that converts `{0}` to `{{0}}` in `ThemeResource` or in the UI code. Keep `{{0}}`/`{{1}}`/`{{2}}` here and use i18next plurals if you need the singular form. The MessageFormat version only belongs in the FreeMarker-rendered `themes/.../base/*` bundles.

Anchor violation message omits key and file

`Didn't find anchor tag <...> in original string` doesn't say which file or key failed. Across dozens of bundles that makes the build failure hard to track down; the `Illegal HTML` message at line 111 does include both. Add `key` (already passed in) and `file`. Also, `santizeAnchors` walks the English anchors in order (line 154), so a correct translation that puts two links in a different order is rejected. If that is intended, say so in the Javadoc at line 148.

Missing English counterpart throws RuntimeException instead of a verifier message

The English path is built with an unanchored `replaceAll` on the absolute path (lines 74-75). When that file doesn't exist, the code throws a bare `RuntimeException`, while the rest of `verify()` reports problems through `messages` or `MojoExecutionException`. A bundle without an `_en` sibling therefore crashes the plugin with a stack trace and no actionable message. The test fixture had to be renamed from `duplicate_keys.properties` to `duplicateKeys_en.properties` for the same reason. Consider adding a message, or throwing `MojoExecutionException`, that names the expected English file.

isAccessTokenId never checks the grant shortcut: indices are off by one and the comparison is inverted

`encodeTokenId` writes sessionType (chars 0-1), tokenType (2-3), then grant (4-5) (`DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:114-117`, and the comment at line 78). `substring(3, 5)` takes the last char of the token type plus the first char of the grant, so for `onrtac` it returns `ta` and never equals `ac`. The guard also returns `false` when the strings *are* equal, so even with the right indices a correct grant would fail the match. As written, the matcher accepts any `xxxxxx:<uuid>` id whatever its grant type, so the expectCodeToToken / expectDeviceCodeToToken / expectRefresh / expectAuthReqIdToToken assertions don't check what they claim to. Fix: `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`. It would also help to check `items[0].length() == 6`.

rawTokenId null check validates grantType a second time

Line 73 calls `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")`, so `rawTokenId` is never validated. A null raw id is accepted, and `encodeTokenId` then silently produces `xxxxxx:null` (`DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:117`). It should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...)`.

New abstract getShortcut() breaks existing custom grant-type factories at startup

`DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit` calls `getShortcut()` on every deployed `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` (`DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:70-77`). A custom grant factory compiled against the previous SPI has no such method, so it throws `AbstractMethodError` during postInit and server startup fails. A custom factory that returns null puts a null key into a `ConcurrentHashMap`, which throws an NPE. You could add a default implementation (for example, derived from the id), or catch the failure and fall back to `na`, so existing extensions keep working.

grantType is captured once in the constructor and not updated by setFormParams; the copy constructor was removed

`grantType` is read from `formParams` only in the constructor. `setFormParams` (line 105) replaces the params without refreshing it, so a caller that swaps the form params gets a stale grant type in the token id. The PR also removes the public `Context(Context)` copy constructor from this SPI class. No caller in the repository uses it, but extensions that do will no longer compile.

Nothing marks a federated recovery code as used

For a local credential, using a code removes it: `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.isValid` calls `removeRecoveryAuthnCode()` and `updateStoredCredential` (RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.java:110-111). For a federated user, `UserCredentialManager.isValid` asks the storage validator first, and once that accepts the input the local provider never runs (UserCredentialManager.java:66-79). The authenticator then reads the federated credential here, but it never tells the storage that a code was spent. So whether a code is single-use depends entirely on each storage provider.

The numbering breaks too. The login bean and this method use `getNextRecoveryAuthnCode()`, which always returns `codes.get(0)` (RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.java:36-41). A provider that rebuilds the model from the remaining codes with `createFromValues` renumbers them from 1 (RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.java:65-67). The user is then asked for "code #1" on every login, even after it was used, which does not match the list they printed.

The reference provider in this PR shows the result: it accepts any of the 12 codes and never removes any (BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:340), so one code works forever.

Fix: after the storage validates a code, have the core consume it (for example, a defined update call that takes the used code or the code index). Or document and enforce the contract that the storage must consume the code and keep the original numbering.

`removeStoredCredentialById` targets the local store for a federated credential

`getCredential` can now return a credential from the user storage, but when all codes are used the code still calls `credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(id)`. That only touches the local store (UserCredentialManager.java:114-117), so the federated credential is left in place and `isConfiguredFor` keeps returning true from the storage. For a federated credential, use `disableCredentialType(RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE)`, as CredentialDeleteHelper.java:64-69 does.

Federated path drops the user label and generation time

The `UserCredentialModel` passed to the storage only carries the JSON list of raw codes. The `generatedUserLabel` and `generatedAt` that the required action put into `credentialModel` (RecoveryAuthnCodesAction.java:110) are not passed on. The test provider fills in `Time.currentTimeMillis()` and no label, so a federated credential differs from a local one in the account console. Consider passing the label and creation time to the storage too.

Hard-coded provider id, looked up even when not used

The literal `"keycloak-recovery-authn-codes"` copies `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProviderFactory.PROVIDER_ID` (RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProviderFactory.java:11), which this module cannot import. That makes it a silent break point if the id ever changes. The provider is also resolved even when the storage accepts the credential. Consider moving the lookup into the `else` branch and adding a comment that ties the literal to the factory constant, or using `createCredentialThroughProvider`.

Federated recovery-codes credential has no id

`createFromValues` never sets an id (RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.java:58-80), and `getCredentials` does not copy `myUser.recoveryCodes.getId()` onto the model. The id is generated at line 195 but then lost. As a result, `CredentialDeleteHelper` cannot match the credential by id (CredentialDeleteHelper.java:64), and the authenticator's `removeStoredCredentialById(getId())` gets null. Set the id from the stored model.

Test never checks that a used code cannot be reused

`testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin` logs in once with code 0 and stops. The provider it runs against accepts any stored code and never consumes one (BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:340). A second login with the same code would succeed, and the test would not notice. Add a second login that expects the next code number and rejects the reused code. That covers the single-use guarantee recovery codes are supposed to provide.

Operator guide says the Operator fails without `rolling-updates`, but no operator code checks it

The CAUTION says the Operator "will fail" when the `rolling-updates` feature is off. Enabling the feature in the test CR exercises nothing in the operator

The feature is enabled only when a strategy is set (the null case returns at line 106). Exit code 4 changes meaning from 'recreate required' to 'feature disabled'

Before this change, `check` exited with 4 when a recreate was needed. It now exits with 3, and 4 means the feature is disabled. getClientsWithPermission can never return per-client grants and returns the type name "Clients" instead

`findByType(server, "Clients", ...)` only matches resources whose type is set. The per-client resources that `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` creates (AdminPermissionsSchema.java:104-110) never call `setType`. Only the type-level resource built in `init` (AdminPermissionsSchema.java:249-250) has type `Clients`, and its name is `Clients`. So this method skips every per-client permission. When an all-clients permission matches, it puts the literal string "Clients" into the set where a client id should go. With V2 on, deleting a client no longer cleans up its V2 resource and permissions

`ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` and `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` are versions 1 and 2 of the same feature (Profile.java:56,58), so only one can be on at a time. Dead code: getEvaluationContext, logger and the TOKEN_EXCHANGE import are never used

Nothing calls `getEvaluationContext` (token exchange throws `UnsupportedOperationException` at line 149). The `logger` at line 51 and the static import of `TOKEN_EXCHANGE` at line 46 are also unused, along with the `Scope`, `EvaluationContext`, `ClientModelIdentity` and `DefaultEvaluationContext` imports that only exist for that method.
